hypothesis_verdicts.hypothesis: H1: the memory map is reprogrammed at runtime, so the boot-time map differs from the steady-state map
hypothesis_verdicts.reasoning: PROVEN, re-derived from bytes I read myself. kn5000_table_data.rom @0x1FB6BE holds `47 00 0c 00 00 | 40 dc fe ff 00 | 34 4b 01 | ec 12 | e9 ee 00 | e9 ee 00 | b4 00 80 | b0 d8` = LD XSP,0xC00 / LD XWA,0x00FFFEDC / LDW IX,0x014B / EXTZ XIX / SLL 0,XBC x2 / LD (XIX),0x80 / JP (XWA). 0x014B is MSAR2. The proof that this is a real remap does not depend on any decode rule: (a) the code executing the store is TABLE-DATA content living at CPU 0xFFB6D3 -- the program flash is 0xFF over that whole region (I checked 0x1FB6B0-0x1FB6DF = all FF); (b) the jump target 0xFFFEDC reads `FF FF FF FF` in the table-data image but `1b 0f 05 ef` = JP 0xEF050F in the program image. So the device answering 0xFFxxxx demonstrably differs before and after that one store. Two such sites exist per image (table_data 0x9FB6D3 and 0x9FC806; program 0xEF4B4B), all writing 0x80; MSAR2 is set to 0xC0 only in the one-time init block. I additionally re-ran an exhaustive binary scan for `F1 <lo> <hi> 00 <imm8>` over SFR 0x140-0x157 across all eight images and reproduce the investigators' inventory exactly (26/26/26/26/0/26/24/0). So the map changes exactly ONCE per CPU, at the bootloader->program-flash handover, and it is CS2 that moves. Felipe's general claim is correct and MAME models none of it (tmp94c241.cpp: m_msar/m_mamr appear only in the ctor, save_item, device_reset and the plain accessors -- I re-grepped).
hypothesis_verdicts.discriminating_test: None needed -- it is proven from ROM bytes. If a live check is still wanted: in MAME, patch the reset PC to 0xFFFEE0 with table_data mapped at the top and confirm the machine only reaches 0xEF050F after the MSAR2 store; on hardware, scope /CS2 across the store.

hypothesis_verdicts.hypothesis: H2: the IC19 dump was taken under a different memory map, which explains the missing payload region
hypothesis_verdicts.reasoning: Refuted in every form I can construct, by measurement. (i) ROTATION/OFFSET form: I re-derived the eight style-section base offsets from the program ROM itself (file 0x116A57: LDA XWA,0x300000 then ADD XBC #0x19800/0x30000/0x49800/0x60000/0x79800/0x90000/0xB0000) and the marker `48 00 4B 00` occurs in the 1 MB dump at EXACTLY 0x000000/0x019800/0x030000/0x049800/0x060000/0x079800/0x090000/0x0B0000 and nowhere else -- 8 for 8, zero spurious. Plus the wallpaper 0x00 run starts exactly at 0x0C0000 with length 77824 = 320*240+1024, and the registration magic 'HK \0' sits exactly at 0x0D3000. A read taken at a different base, rotated, or wrapped cannot produce all ten anchors. (ii) WINDOW form: MSAR5/MAMR5 = 0x00/0xFF are written once, inside the single init block, in table_data, v7, v9, v10, ic30 and the payload, and NEVER rewritten anywhere in eight images (my own scan). IC19 and the HD-AE5000 ROM contain zero CS writes in any encoding. The CS5 window is fixed, and it is independently corroborated by the driver's schematic-derived comment `IC14 (A22=1 and CS5)`, which only makes sense if CS5 spans 0x000000-0x7FFFFF. (iii) REGION-4 TWO-DIE form: the last non-FF byte is at chip 0x0D344F, i.e. inside the UPPER 512 KB die (>= 0x380000), so both dies were read. What survives of Felipe's hypothesis is its general half (H1), not its application to IC19. NOTE: the one place where a boot-time-vs-steady-state distinction genuinely bites is the constant 0x800000 -- pre-handover it is the PROGRAM flash, post-handover the TABLE-DATA pair -- but that is CS2/CS4, not CS5, and does not touch IC19.
hypothesis_verdicts.discriminating_test: On the real unit, open the built-in memory-dump screen (DBMEMORYDUMPPROC, symbol at 0xFA2EE6) at address 0x3E0000 and look for the ASCII 'SLIDE4K'. If it is there, the dump -- not the map -- is what is wrong. No desoldering, no tooling.

hypothesis_verdicts.hypothesis: H3: the IC19 region genuinely was never programmed on this unit (no Program DATA FILE PCK update was ever applied)
hypothesis_verdicts.reasoning: Split it into three variants, because they do not stand or fall together. H3a 'the two staging sectors were blank IN THE CHIP at the moment of the dump' -- SUPPORTED (strong): the image is a genuine chip read (the 77,824-byte block of 0x00 at 0x0C0000 can only be actively programmed data; flash erases to 0xFF), and 0x0E0000-0x0FFFFF is sector-clean under both the top-boot and bottom-boot AM29F400/800 maps. H3b 'no 007h update was EVER applied' -- UNDECIDED. The measured state (every sector written except exactly the two the 007h handler erases) is equally consistent with (1) never installed, (2) a 007h install whose erase phase completed and whose write phase did not, and (3) a dump truncated at 0x0E0000 and 0xFF-padded, which is byte-indistinguishable from (1). The w6-ic19-model argument that the data stopping at a DATA boundary favours 'never programmed' does not work: the last non-FF byte tells you where the data ended, not where the dump ended. H3c 'this unit worked in the dumped state' -- REFUTED by the firmware. I re-measured the gate byte: program[0x1FFEED] = 0xFF in v7, v9 AND v10, and the v10 image on the update floppy decodes to the same file, so every dumped firmware takes the IC19@0x3E0000 branch. I also measured the fallback source: table_data[0x000000..0xFF] is an LE32 pointer table (0x800088, 0x802D10, 0x805998, ...) and 0x100.. is 0xF7 filler. So a machine in the dumped state would ship 192 KB of filler over the latches and then `call 0x400` into a pointer table -- no sound. Since Felipe's unit works, the IC19 image we hold is NOT the state of that machine while it was working. That is the real open question, and it is a PROVENANCE question, not a memory-map question.
hypothesis_verdicts.discriminating_test: Two questions to Felipe, both free: (1) was that keyboard producing sound at the time he dumped IC19, or was the sub-CPU already dead? (2) Read 0x3E0000 today on the unit via the built-in memory-dump screen and report whether 'SLIDE4K' is present. Either answer collapses H3b immediately; a full re-read of 0x300000-0x3FFFFF settles the truncation variant.

hypothesis_verdicts.hypothesis: H4: the sub-CPU payload could be resident in the undumped 116 KB of IC30
hypothesis_verdicts.reasoning: Three independent kills, in decreasing order of strength. (1) WIRING: the payload is sourced by the MAIN CPU from ITS OWN address space -- I disassembled SubCPU_Send_Payload myself (program file 0x0F0680, base 0xEF0680): XIZ is either 0x50000 (main DRAM, holding the decompressed IC19 image) or 0x800000 (table data), and the four InterCPU_E1_Bulk_Transfer calls move XIZ+0x100->sub 0xF000 (0x10000), XIZ+0x10100->0x1F000 (0x10000), XIZ+0x20100->0x2F000 (0xFF00) and XIZ+0->0x400 (0x100). IC30 is not in the main CPU's address space at all; the CPUs share only the 8-bit latches (main 0x140000 / sub 0x120000). No path exists. (2) ARITHMETIC: 0x10000+0x10000+0xFF00+0x100 = 0x30000 = 196,608 bytes; the whole IC30 is 131,072 bytes and only 116,736 are undumped. (Even the compressed 93,203-byte form, which WOULD fit, is dead on arrival: the boot ROM has no decompressor and the main CPU unconditionally overwrites sub-DRAM 0x400-0x4FF and 0xF000-0x3EEFF before `call 0x400`.) (3) ADDRESSABILITY: under the decode rule that the main-CPU handover forces (see notes), sub-CPU CS2 = MSAR 0xFF / MAMR 0x01 is a 64 KB window at 0xFF0000-0xFFFFFF, not 128 KB at 0xFE0000. I measured that ALL 4,352 non-FF bytes of the IC30 dump lie in file 0x18000-0x1FFFF = CPU 0xFF8000-0xFFFFFF (the top 32 KB), and that the 2 KB Felipe read at 0xFE0000 came back entirely 0xFF -- which on that reading is an UNDECODED read, not evidence about the chip. So the undumped-AND-addressable space is at most ~52 KB, not 116 KB. Note this makes Felipe's testimony (1) safer, not shakier: what he could not reach was probably never reachable by the CPU.
hypothesis_verdicts.discriminating_test: None needed for the payload question. To close the IC30 dump itself with the tooling he already has: re-run subcpu_send.asm over 0xFF0000-0xFF77FF (30 KB) and 0xFF9800-0xFFEFFF (22 KB), and additionally sample 0xFD0000-0xFD07FF as a control -- if the control also reads 0xFF, then '0xFF' is the open-bus value and the 0xFE0000 window carries no information.

hypothesis_verdicts.hypothesis: H5: MAME overlay of the update-floppy payload at custom_data 0x0e0000 is a faithful reconstruction of a post-installation machine
hypothesis_verdicts.reasoning: SUPPORTED for the v10 (and by inheritance v9) BIOS option, proven for every byte the firmware reads; UNDECIDED for the other four options. I re-verified the whole chain myself with an independently written SLIDE4K decoder. The floppy kn5000_v10_disk.img (sha1 a892bedc...) carries HKMSPRG.SLD = two concatenated streams: @0x04800 decodes to 2,097,152 bytes == kn5000_v10_program.rom exactly, consuming 965,545 bytes; @0xF03A9 decodes to 196,608 bytes == kn5000_subprogram_v142.rom exactly, consuming 93,203; 0xF03A9-0x4800 = 965,545 and 965,545+93,203 = 1,058,748 = the FAT12 directory size. disk[0xF03A9 : +93203] is byte-identical to kn5000_subprogram_v142_compressed.rom, i.e. MAME's overlay file was carved from this floppy. The overlay address is right: custom_data is ROM_REGION16_LE(0x100000) mapped by map(0x300000,0x3fffff), so offset 0x0E0000 == CPU 0x3E0000, which is exactly what the boot consumer reads (CP (0xFFFEED),0xFF / LD XWA,0x3E0000 / CALL SLIDE_Parse_Header, re-disassembled at 0xEF0704). The only deviation from a real install is the tail: an install writes 0x20000 bytes, i.e. the 93,203-byte stream + 68 x 0x00 + 37,801 x 0xE5 (the installer over-reads past EOF), where MAME leaves 0xFF -- and my decoder consumes exactly 93,203 input bytes, so not one of those 37,869 bytes is ever read. TWO CAVEATS, neither a fidelity defect but both worth stating: (a) the v141->v7/v8 and v140->v5/v6 pairings in kn5000.cpp:1481-1484 are NOT measured -- only the v10 disk exists on this machine, so four of the six BIOS options rest on filename inference; (b) the composite is a reconstruction (a genuine chip dump of a machine that never had the update + a payload carved from a floppy) and nothing in the ROM definition marks it as such -- the base ROM_LOAD carries a clean CRC/SHA1 and the ROMX_LOAD overlay carries no BAD_DUMP. Since custom_data is a ROM region, the emulated machine can also never run an install.
hypothesis_verdicts.discriminating_test: Dump 0x3E0000-0x3FFFFF from a real post-install unit (memory-dump screen or the homebrew reader) and compare against wave6/w6-update-disks/ic19_3e0000_postinstall.bin. For the unverified pairings, the cheap version is to ask Felipe whether he has v5-v8 update disks, or to check whether the v140/v141 compressed files are byte-slices of any disk image he still holds.

refuted_findings.claim: "NEGATIVE RESULT / OPEN CONTRADICTION: under the calibrated rule, the main CPU's handoff write MSAR2 0xC0 -> 0x80 is a NO-OP ... either the TMP94C241's decode is not the simple mask rule, or an external glue element on the KN5000 board is triggered by that bus cycle." (w6-csregs)
refuted_findings.why: WRONG, and it is the assumed decode rule that is wrong, not the hardware. The premise is 'MAMR bit k masks A(16+k)' (64 KB granularity), calibrated on a single sub-CPU data point. Take instead the 32 KB granularity reading -- size = 32 KB x (MAMR+1), i.e. MAMR bit k masks A(15+k) while MSAR bit k is A(16+k) -- and MAMR2 = 0x7F is a 4 MB window with only A23 and A22 compared: MSAR2 = 0xC0 gives 0xC00000-0xFFFFFF, MSAR2 = 0x80 gives 0x800000-0xBFFFFF. That is a real swap, and it is over-determined by four independent facts. (1) It is REQUIRED: 0xFFFEDC holds FF FF FF FF in the table-data image and JP 0xEF050F in the program image, so the decode MUST change. (2) It predicts the firmware's alias constant exactly: a 2 MB device inside a 4 MB window appears at base+0 and base+0x200000, so ROM offset X is at 0xE00000+X before and 0x800000+X after -- delta 0x600000, which is literally the `+ 0x600000` in boot_cpserial.s and the 0x9Fxxxx <-> 0xFFxxxx pairing. (3) It makes CS4 (MSAR 0x80 / MAMR 0xFF = 8 MB at A23=1) and CS5 (MSAR 0x00 / MAMR 0xFF = 8 MB at A23=0) tile the whole 16 MB, with CS2 carving its 4 MB out of CS4's half -- so the program flash occupies whichever half CS2 is not in, mirrored twice, which is exactly why 0xFFFEDC and 0xEF____ both work post-handover. (4) It puts CS5 at 0x000000-0x7FFFFF, which is the only reading under which the driver's independent schematic-derived comment `IC14 (A22=1 and CS5)` makes sense. No external glue is needed and none should be invented.

refuted_findings.claim: Two investigators calibrated MSAR/MAMR with mutually incompatible rules and BOTH claimed exact confirmation from the same MAME map.
refuted_findings.why: w6-bootpath: 'sub CS3 00/1F -> 1 MB = DRAM IC28/IC29 ... nine independent agreements ... the 64 KB-granularity alternative fails three of these' (32 KB rule). w6-ic30-audit: 'MSAR3=0x00/MAMR3=0x0F gives exactly 0x000000-0x0FFFFF = 1 MB ... two independent exact hits' (64 KB rule). The boot ROM writes MAMR3 = 0x1F or 0x0F by strap, so at most one of these can be the 1 MB case. Both agents fitted the rule to the answer they wanted and then reported the fit as confirmation. The orchestrator should treat every address-range table in wave 6 as an INTERPRETATION, and should adopt only the constraint that is rule-independent: CS2 moves between 0xC00000-0xFFFFFF and 0x800000-0xBFFFFF at the handover, everything else is static.

refuted_findings.claim: "sub CS2 FF/01 -> 0xFE0000-0xFFFFFF = 128 KB = IC30 ... two independent exact hits" (w6-ic30-audit), and the derived headline "116,736 bytes (89.06%) are undumped".
refuted_findings.why: The 128 KB fit requires the 64 KB rule, which is refuted by the main-CPU handover (same silicon, same registers). Under the rule the handover forces, sub CS2 = 0xFF0000-0xFFFFFF = 64 KB. Two measurements agree with that and not with 128 KB: ALL 4,352 non-FF bytes of the dump lie in file 0x18000-0x1FFFF = CPU 0xFF8000-0xFFFFFF, and the 2 KB Felipe read at 0xFE0000 came back entirely 0xFF -- an undecoded read, not a blank ROM. So the honest headline is 'at most ~52 KB is both addressable and undumped', and MAME's map(0xfe0000,0xffffff) for the subcpu region is over-generous. This strengthens rather than weakens Felipe's testimony (1).

refuted_findings.claim: "MAME's static map is ACCIDENTALLY correct: it equals the post-handover steady state." (w6-bootpath)
refuted_findings.why: Right in substance, incomplete in detail. Post-handover, CS4's residue is 0xC00000-0xFFFFFF holding the 2 MB program flash MIRRORED TWICE (0xC00000 and 0xE00000). kn5000.cpp maps only map(0xe00000,0xffffff).mask(0x1fffff) -- the 0xC00000-0xDFFFFF mirror is absent. Anything the firmware reaches through the lower mirror would fault in MAME and works on hardware. Cheap check before anyone relies on the 'accidentally correct' framing: scan the program and table-data images for 24-bit immediates in 0xC00000-0xDFFFFF.

refuted_findings.claim: "LZ_Decompress_Init's destination is the 0x800000 window ... so the 0x800000-0x9FFFFF window must be pointed at the main-program flash pair during that operation" -- offered as "independent, disk-backed support for Felipe (2)" (w6-update-disks).
refuted_findings.why: The observation is correct but the inference adds a remap that is not needed. The table-data bootloader's copy of the updater runs BEFORE the single known MSAR2 handover, and pre-handover 0x800000-0xBFFFFF is already the program-flash pair (2 MB, so 0x800000 and 0x900000 are its two halves -- which is exactly why disc type 001h writes 1 MB to each). The program-flash copy runs after the handover, where 0x800000-0x9FFFFF is the table-data pair -- which is what disc types 003h/008h need. 'Two updaters, each programming the chip the other executes from' therefore follows from H1 alone; it is evidence for H1, not for H2. One genuine open item this exposes: the PROGRAM-FLASH copy of the 007h handler decompresses stream 1 (the 2 MB main program) to 0x800000, which post-handover is the table-data pair. Either that handler is unreachable (updates always enter through the bootloader, which owns the boot FDC driver at 0x9FD8A5) or there is a second remap nobody has found. Settle this before building a dynamic-map model.

refuted_findings.claim: "The blank tail is sector-clean and the written data stops at a DATA boundary, not a transfer boundary -- which favours 'never programmed' over 'truncated dump'." (w6-ic19-model)
refuted_findings.why: Overstated. The last non-FF byte marks where the DATA ended, not where the DUMP ended. A dump truncated anywhere in 0x0D3450-0x0FFFFF and 0xFF-padded is byte-identical to a complete dump of a chip that was never programmed there; the file cannot distinguish them and neither can any statistic computed from it. What genuinely does survive is (a) the image is a real chip read (the 77,824-byte 0x00 wallpaper block proves programmed-to-zero content) and (b) the blank region is exactly the two sectors the 007h handler erases -- which is suggestive but is equally the signature of an interrupted install.

refuted_findings.claim: "BxCSH bit 7 looks like a per-block enable." (w6-csregs, self-graded speculative)
refuted_findings.why: Contradicted by the local reference: .claude/skills/tmp94c241/references/sfr.md documents BnCSH as bit6 = BnREC, bits5-4 = BnOM, bits1-0 = BnBUS, with bit7 unassigned. Under that layout every written value decodes sensibly and cross-checks the board: B2CSH 0xC2 = 32-bit (table-data pair, ROM_LOAD32_WORD), B4CSH 0x82 = 32-bit (program-flash pair, unlock at 0x815554/0x80AAA8 = 4x word address), B5CSH 0x81 = 16-bit (IC19 single x16, unlock at 0xAAAA/0x5554 = 2x word address), B0CSH 0x80 = 8-bit (IC21 SRAM), sub B2CSH 0xC0 = 8-bit (IC30 mask ROM). That is five independent agreements and it should replace the bit-7 speculation.

refuted_findings.claim: technics-docs/system-update-discs.md:187 -- "For type 7, the compressed program ROM is written to Custom Data Flash at 0x3E0000. On next boot, the decompressor reads from this staging area and programs the actual Program Flash at 0xE00000."
refuted_findings.why: Wrong, and it is a published doc so it will keep re-infecting future waves. What is written to 0x3E0000 is the compressed SUB-CPU payload (stream 2 of the .SLD, 93,203 bytes, decodes to the 196,608-byte kn5000_subprogram_v142.rom -- I decoded it), and it is read on EVERY boot by SubCPU_Send_Payload, not once. The main program image is stream 1 and is decompressed straight into the program flash through the 0x800000 window during the install. The staging area is permanent, not transient -- which is precisely why H5 works.

verdicts.notes:
SUMMARY FOR THE ORCHESTRATOR

Verdicts: H1 SUPPORTED (proven) - H2 REFUTED - H3 UNDECIDED (split into 3 variants; H3a supported, H3b undecided, H3c refuted) - H4 REFUTED - H5 SUPPORTED for the v10 BIOS only.

The wave-6 corpus is substantially sound. Its factual core - the CS-write inventory, the handoff instruction, the IC19 alignment anchors, the update-disk decode, the IC30 census, the MAME gap analysis - reproduced exactly when I re-derived it from the bytes. Everything I overturned is INTERPRETATION layered on top: the MSAR/MAMR decode rule, and one published doc error.

THE DECODE RULE, settled well enough to build on (strong, not proven - no datasheet exists on this machine):
  block size = 32 KB x (MAMR+1); MSAR bit k = A(16+k); MAMR bit k masks A(15+k); low MSAR bits below the window size are ignored.
  MAIN CPU: CS0 512K@0x180000 (IC21 SRAM mirrors in the top), CS1 2M@0, CS2 4M@0xC00000 -> 4M@0x800000 AT THE HANDOVER,
            CS3 1M@0 (DRAM IC9/IC10), CS4 8M@0x800000 (program pair, visible in whatever CS2 vacates, mirrored x2),
            CS5 8M@0x000000 (IC19 at 0x300000, IC14 at A22=1 - matches the driver's schematic comment).
  SUB CPU:  CS0 256K@0x100000, CS1 128K@0x100000, CS2 64K@0xFF0000 (IC30), CS3 1M@0 strap-selectable to 512K,
            CS4 64K@0x120000 (latches), CS5 64K@0x130000 (DSP regs).
  The rule is pinned by four things that must all hold simultaneously: the 0xFFFEDC byte difference, the firmware's
  +0x600000 alias constants, the CS4/CS5 tiling of the full 16 MB, and the BnCSH bus widths matching the actual chips.

WHAT THIS MEANS FOR THE ORIGINAL PROBLEM (where is the sub-CPU payload):
  The memory-map hypothesis is DEAD as an explanation. The payload is missing for a provenance reason, not a decode
  reason. All dumped firmwares (v7/v9/v10, and the v10 image on the floppy) gate on program[0x1FFEED] = 0xFF and take
  the IC19@0x3E0000 branch; the fallback at table_data 0x800100 is 0xF7 filler behind an LE32 pointer table. A machine
  in the state of our dumps could not run its sub-CPU. So either that IC19 read is incomplete, or the chip was in a
  post-erase / never-installed state at dump time and the instrument was not making sound then. Only Felipe can
  distinguish these, and the built-in memory-dump screen (DBMEMORYDUMPPROC 0xFA2EE6) at 0x3E0000 does it in a minute.

RECOMMENDED SEQUENCING (my view, unsolicited but cheap):
  1. Ask Felipe the two H3 questions. Everything else about the payload is blocked on the answer.
  2. Do NOT build a dynamic chip-select model yet. The single behaviour that matters is one CS2 window swap; a
     memory_view with two states (table-data-high / program-high) reproduces it, and the driver's runtime
     space.install_device() for the HD-AE5000 slot will need to move inside the view.
  3. Before that, resolve the program-flash-copy 007h contradiction noted in the refutations - it is the only thing
     that could imply a SECOND remap, and it would change the view's shape.

ARTIFACT: /home/fsanches/.claude/jobs/d0e1b1c2/tmp/wave6/w7-adjudicator/reverification.txt - every measurement above,
with file offsets, so none of it has to be re-run.

FIRMWARE / HARDWARE / MAME boundary, stated explicitly as required:
  FIRMWARE does: program all six CS blocks once per CPU, then move CS2 exactly once at the handover.
  HARDWARE does: decode those windows (rule above, reconstructed not documented); a sub-CPU Port-G strap selects the
    DRAM size; the reset-default map is unknown and is constrained only weakly (Boot_Init touches no external memory
    before the CS block and loads no stack pointer until after it).
  MAME MODELS: none of the decode. It stores MSAR/MAMR/BnCS and ignores them, boots at 0xEF03C6 instead of running the
    table-data first-stage bootloader at all, and hardcodes a static map that happens to equal the post-handover steady
    state except for the missing 0xC00000-0xDFFFFF program-flash mirror.

hypothesis_verdicts.hypothesis: The chip-select (MSAR/MAMR/BnCS) registers are never written by the firmware — 'a text grep for writes to those registers in v10/maincpu found NOTHING'.
hypothesis_verdicts.reasoning: PROVEN WRONG BY FILE:LINE. All 24 memory-controller registers are programmed in one contiguous block at /home/fsanches/compartilhado/kn5000-roms-disasm/v10/maincpu/shared/boot_hw_init.s:85-134 (identical files exist in v7, v9 and table_data/shared/boot_hw_init.s). The grep missed them because the disassembler emits the direct address in DECIMAL: `stdi8 (323), 30` is MSAR0(0x143)=0x1E, `(327)`=MSAR1(0x147)=0x10, `(331)`=MSAR2(0x14B)=0xC0, `(335)`=MSAR3(0x14F)=0x00, `(339)`=MSAR4(0x153)=0x80, `(343)`=MSAR5(0x157)=0x00; masks `(322)`=MAMR0=0x0F, `(326)`=MAMR1=0x3F, `(330)`=MAMR2=0x7F, `(334)`=MAMR3=0x1F, `(338)`=MAMR4=0xFF, `(342)`=MAMR5=0xFF; then BnCSL `(320,324,328,332,336,340)` = 0x11,0x33,0x11,0x22,0x11,0x22 and BnCSH `(321,325,329,333,337,341)` = 0x80,0x81,0xC2,0x8A,0x82,0x81. The firmware's own inline comments name the blocks: Block0@0x1E0000 (IC21 SRAM), Block1@0x100000 (I/O), Block2@0xC00000, Block3@0x000000 (DRAM), Block4@0x800000 (Table Data), Block5@0x000000/mask 0xFF (catch-all).
hypothesis_verdicts.discriminating_test: Already settled — read boot_hw_init.s:85-134. Re-grep any future SFR question with the DECIMAL address form (0x140-0x157 = 320-343), not the hex form or the symbolic name.

hypothesis_verdicts.hypothesis: MAME does not emulate the KN5000's dynamic memory map, and whether one exists is unknown.
hypothesis_verdicts.reasoning: The remap is PROVEN and was already documented in the disassembly repo — no investigator cited it. Normal cold boot: table_data/kn5000_table_data.s:1253-1258 `Boot_PrepareJump` does `ld xwa, 0xFFFEDC; ldw ix, 0x14B ; CS2 register; ld (xix), 0x80 ; CS2 config; jp (xwa)` — a runtime write of 0x80 to MSAR2, changing CS2's window from 0xC00000 to 0x800000, immediately before jumping into the program flash. The factory/HDAE path does the same at table_data/kn5000_table_data.s:3577-3579 (jumping to 0xFFFED8). The repo states the consequence explicitly: table_data/boot_clib.s:7-9 'At reset the table-data ROM is mapped at 0xE00000-0xFFFFFF; after the CS2 remap it appears at 0x800000-0x9FFFFF', and table_data/kn5000_table_data.s:1116-1118 says the same. MAME (kn5000.cpp:575-576) maps table_data statically at 0x800000 with .mirror(0x200000) and program statically at 0xE00000 — the mirror is itself corroboration that MAMR2=0x7F is a 4 MB block (0x800000-0xBFFFFF after the remap). I also measured the two chips DIFFER at these addresses: maincpu file 0x1FFEE0 = `1b c6 03 ef 0e c2 e8 ff ff 27 0e ff ff ff 00 ff`, table_data file 0x1FFEE0 = `1b e8 b4 ff 0e ff ff ff ff ff ff ff ff ff 00 00`. So 0xFFFEEF = 0xFF in program flash but 0x00 in table data — and SubCPU_Send_Payload's first guard is `cpib_da (0xFFFEEF), 0xff; jrl nz, Done`. Real machines DO ship the payload, therefore the CS2 remap has already happened by then (a hard, byte-grounded constraint on boot ordering that nobody stated).
hypothesis_verdicts.discriminating_test: Model it: give kn5000.cpp a tmp94c241 memory-controller callback that installs table_data at 0xC00000-0xFFFFFF at reset and moves it to 0x800000-0xBFFFFF on the MSAR2 write, and confirm the machine still boots identically. If it does, the static map is a coincidence-of-content, not a fidelity claim.

hypothesis_verdicts.hypothesis: Felipe may have dumped IC19 while it was mapped at a different address range, because the TMP94C241 can reassign chip-selects at runtime.
hypothesis_verdicts.reasoning: The general phenomenon is real (CS2 remap, above), but the specific mechanism looks unavailable for IC19. IC19 sits under CS5, and CS5 is programmed as the CATCH-ALL: MSAR5=0x00 with MAMR5=0xFF (all address bits don't-care). Changing MSAR5 therefore cannot move IC19. The IC19-vs-IC14-vs-other split is done by DISCRETE LOGIC, which I read off the service manual (physical evidence nobody had consulted): SM page 32 'CPU SECTION (A) P.C. Diagram' shows IC11 TC74VHC138F 3-to-8 decoder with A0<-net A16 (pin1), A1<-net A17 (pin2), A2<-net A18 (pin3) and its three enables labelled /CS2 (pin4), /CS3 (pin5, tied to GND), CS1 (pin6); IC12 T7W139F 2-to-4 decoder with A<-net A19 (pin1); IC13 TC74VHC139F dual 2-to-4 with net A22 (pin2) plus nets A20 and A19. IC19 itself is QVIGFKN5KAX1 '8M BIT CUSTOM DATA ROM', x16 (BYTE pin33 tied to +5D), 19 address pins AD0..AD18 fed by nets A1..A19, /CE pin12, /OE pin14, /WE pin43. So IC19's address window is fixed by A19-A23 through IC12/IC13, not by CPU registers. This does NOT refute Felipe's testimony about what he did — only the proposed explanation. The only *runtime* CS write outside boot is `stdi8 (340), 102` (B5CSL 0x154 := 0x66, boot value 0x22) at v10/maincpu/boot/system_handlers.s:8027 and :8211 and table_data/kn5000_table_data.s:3477 — all three immediately before touching the HD-AE5000 PPI/flash, so almost certainly a wait-state/width change, not a relocation.
hypothesis_verdicts.discriminating_test: Trace two nets on service-manual page 32 to their source: IC19 pin 12 (/CE) and pin 14 (/OE). If both terminate on an IC12/IC13 decoder output whose inputs are only A19-A23 and the CPU's CS5, IC19 is physically unrelocatable and the hypothesis is dead. (Crops already rendered: /home/fsanches/.claude/jobs/d0e1b1c2/tmp/wave6/critic/c_ic19.png, c_dec.png, c_ic11.png, c_band.png; full-res page at raw32-000.png, 9921x7008.)

hypothesis_verdicts.hypothesis: The payload-source marker byte differs across firmware versions, which would be decisive.
hypothesis_verdicts.reasoning: It is byte-identical in all three images we hold. ROM_PaddingFF is at 0xFFFEEB (= file offset 0x1FFEEB in the 2 MB maincpu image). Measured: kn5000_v10_program.rom, kn5000_v9_program.rom and kn5000_v7_program.rom ALL read `ff ff ff 00 ff` at 0x1FFEEB..0x1FFEEF. Hence ROM_PaddingFF_0x2 (0xFFFEED) = 0xFF in v7/v9/v10 -> `jr nz` NOT taken -> the IC19 path is taken on every firmware we have; ROM_PaddingFF_0x4 (0xFFFEEF) = 0xFF -> the payload transfer is not skipped; ROM_PaddingFF_0x3 (0xFFFEEE) = 0x00 -> Boot_CallInitHandlers' `cpib_da (0xFFFEEE),0xff` fails and the four init handlers at 0xFFFEF0 are NEVER called. I also diffed the routine bodies: v7 kn5000_v7_program.s:313-356 vs v10 kn5000_v10_program.s:316-359 are IDENTICAL apart from symbolisation (v7 emits the raw `cpib_da (0xfffeef)` / `(0xfffeed)`). So the chooser is unchanged v7->v10.
hypothesis_verdicts.discriminating_test: Only v5/v6 could still move this: MAME references kn5000_v5_program.rom (CRC 0xfbd035e3) and kn5000_v6_program.rom (CRC 0x0205db30), which are NOT in original_ROMs/. Obtain either and read one byte at file offset 0x1FFEED. If it is non-FF, candidate A (table_data 0x800100) was the live path on early boards and the whole 'neither candidate has the payload' puzzle is a generation skew.

hypothesis_verdicts.hypothesis: Neither candidate source contains the payload, so something is fundamentally wrong with our understanding of the boot path.
hypothesis_verdicts.reasoning: The IC19 side is fully closed end-to-end; only the IC19 DUMP is missing the data. (a) v10/maincpu/boot/system_handlers.s:7758-7770, `HANDLE_UPDATE_FILE_TYPE_ID_007h` — '; "Technics KN5000 Program DATA FILE PCK"' — does `lds wa,1; ld xbc,0x3e0000; call Flash_EraseSectorWithBankSelect; lds wa,1; ld xbc,0x3f0000; call Flash_EraseSectorWithBankSelect; calr Flash_BurnWithProgress; calr LZ_Decompress_Init; calr LZSS_Decompress_ToFlash`. So the update disk erases IC19 sectors 0x3E0000 and 0x3F0000 and LZSS-decompresses into them. (b) /home/fsanches/compartilhado/kn5000_project/kn5000_v10_disk.img contains the string 'Technics KN5000 Program  DATA FILE PCK  by T.Nishino' at 0x4200 and a SLIDE4K stream at 0xF03A9. (c) That stream is BYTE-IDENTICAL and CONTIGUOUS with kn5000_subprogram_v142_compressed.rom for all 0x16C13 bytes. (d) Its header decodes as 'SLIDE4K\0' + BE24 size 0x030000 = 196608 = exactly the three transfers 0x10000+0x10000+0xFF00 plus the trailing 0x100. So MAME's ROMX_LOAD at custom_data offset 0x0E0000 is the RIGHT CONTENT at the RIGHT ADDRESS — it is a faithful reconstruction of what the update disk writes, just not a chip image. Separately, candidate A is confirmed dead-on-arrival by bytes: table_data file 0x100 (= 0x800100) is `f7 f7 f7 ... ` preset-bank filler, so if the fallback were ever taken the sub-CPU would be fed garbage.
hypothesis_verdicts.discriminating_test: Already settled. The remaining question is only about the IC19 DUMP, not the boot path.

hypothesis_verdicts.hypothesis: kn5000_subprogram_v142.rom is the correct sub-CPU firmware for a v10 machine (not just 'the file that makes the emulator work').
hypothesis_verdicts.reasoning: Structural cross-validation that nobody performed. The sub-CPU's own reset vector table lives in IC30 at 0xFFFF00 (file 0x1FF00) and reads: slot0 = `e0 fe ff 00` = 0x00FFFEE0 (its reset handler, inside a DUMPED block), then slots pointing at 0x00000405, 0x0000040A, 0x0000040F, 0x00000414, 0x00000419, 0x0000041E, 0x00000423, 0x000004DC (the NMI slot), 0x00000428 ... 0x000004D7 — a 5-byte stride starting at 0x405. SubCPU_Send_Payload's LAST transfer is `ld xwa, xiz; ldw bc, 0x100; ld xde, 0x400` — the FIRST 0x100 bytes of the source go to sub-CPU 0x400. And kn5000_subprogram_v142.rom[0:0x40] = `1b 24 f9 01 0e | 1b bc fb 01 0e | 1b bc fb 01 0e | ...` — exactly 5-byte `jp <24-bit>; ret` trampolines, whose targets (0x01F924, 0x01FBBC, 0x020E86 ...) land inside the sub-CPU RAM range 0xF000-0x3EF00 that the same payload fills. Vector stride, trampoline stride, destination address and jump targets all agree. That is a matched pair with THIS IC30.
hypothesis_verdicts.discriminating_test: Parse all 44 vectors from IC30 file 0x1FF00 and assert payload[v-0x400] == 0x1B (JP opcode) for every one, and max(v) < 0x500. If any vector points outside 0x400-0x4FF, the 0x100-byte transfer size is wrong and the pairing is coincidental.

hypothesis_verdicts.hypothesis: Felipe's IC30 educated guess ('the undumped regions are almost certainly 0xFF, because the dumped code references nothing there') is safe.
hypothesis_verdicts.reasoning: Weaker than stated, and the driver's own description of the dump is imprecise. Measured: only 4352 of 131072 bytes are non-FF, and the non-FF content sits in just two blocks, CPU 0xFF8000-0xFF904C (4173 bytes) and 0xFFFE80-0xFFFFFF (384 bytes). The driver comment (kn5000.cpp:1466) claims the undumped ranges are fe0800-ff7800 and ff9800-fff000, i.e. that fe0000-fe0800, ff7800-ff9800 and fff000-ffffff WERE read — but ~10 KB of those 'read' windows are also 0xFF, so 'dumped and blank' is indistinguishable from 'not dumped' in the file as shipped. A byte scan of the dumped blocks finds 2 of 16 aligned 32-bit intra-ROM values and 42 of 86 24-bit intra-ROM values pointing into the UNDUMPED ranges (e.g. 0xFF42A3, 0xFFCFEB, 0xFEE000, 0xFF0000). Most 24-bit hits are surely coincidence at this data volume, but this has never been checked properly.
hypothesis_verdicts.discriminating_test: Disassemble only the two real blocks (0xFF8000-0xFF904C and 0xFFFE80-0xFFFFFF) with unidasm and enumerate the targets of actual JP/JR/CALL/CALR instructions and the 44 reset-vector entries — not raw byte scans. If every real control-flow target lands in a dumped block, Felipe's guess is corroborated; if even one lands in fe0800-ff7800 or ff9800-fff000, the IC30 dump is provably incomplete in a way that matters.

hypothesis_verdicts.hypothesis: The IC19 dump we hold is a faithful image of the physical IC19 in a working KN5000.
hypothesis_verdicts.reasoning: It contains real, plausible user content, but its internal record grid has an unexplained phase that nobody has examined. Non-FF blocks (>=4 KB FF gap): 0x000000-0x0167FF (0x16800), 0x019800-0x0467FF (0x2D000), 0x049800-0x0767FF (0x2D000), 0x079800-0x0A67FF (0x2D000), 0x0B0000-0x0B005F (0x60), 0x0C0000-0x0D344F (0x13450). The middle three are a perfect grid: body 0x2D000, pad 0x3000, stride 0x30000, and each begins with the same 4-byte magic `48 00 4b 00` (also present at 0x000000 and 0x0B0000). But the FIRST block is 0x16800 = exactly HALF of 0x2D000 and its grid position implies a record starting at chip offset -0x16800. Region 0x0C0000-0x0D344F has entropy 0.10 (essentially zero-filled with sparse structure). The strings are user style names ('Bolero puro', 'GentleSwing 1', 'GospelRevival', 'AccordionJazz') — consistent with 'a system that had it already programmed by the initial data disk' (kn5000.cpp:1474). Sectors 0xE0000-0xFFFFF (= CPU 0x3E0000-0x3FFFFF, the sub-CPU payload) are pure 0xFF, i.e. exactly the two sectors that HANDLE_UPDATE_FILE_TYPE_ID_007h erases — the image looks like a machine on which the PCK file was erased but never (re)written, which cannot boot.
hypothesis_verdicts.discriminating_test: Two cheap ones. (1) Rotate the 1 MB image by ±0x16800 and by ±0x20000 (mod 0x100000) and re-run the record-grid + `48004b00` alignment test; if a rotation makes the first partial record whole, the dump is offset. (2) Ask Felipe the one question that settles provenance: was IC19 read on a chip programmer with the part removed/socketed, or read in-system by the CPU (like IC30)? If in-system, a readback-window limit explains a blank 0xE0000-0xFFFFF far better than an erased chip.

hypothesis_verdicts.hypothesis: kn5000_v10_program.rom is a dump of the physical program flash IC4/IC6.
hypothesis_verdicts.reasoning: Never established, and the KN7000 precedent says this matters. notes/rom-backup-and-update-format.md §2.2 documents that the KN7000 'program ROM' we hold is the UPDATE PAYLOAD (0x3F6F01 of a 0x400000 chip) and that the top ~37 KB — containing the resident updater — is neither shipped nor dumped. The KN5000 has the same update mechanism: HANDLE_UPDATE_FILE_TYPE_ID_001h ('Technics KN5000 Program DATA FILE 1/2') and 003h ('Table DATA FILE 1/2') at v10/maincpu/boot/system_handlers.s:7700-7724 both run Flash_BurnWithProgress + SHOW_FD_TO_FLASH_MEMORY_MESSAGE and reference 0x800000/0x900000. If our v10 image is the floppy payload rather than a chip read, then the marker byte at 0xFFFEED — which sits only 0x13 bytes below the interrupt vector table, i.e. deep inside the region an update rewrites — is the shipped value, not necessarily the on-chip value for a machine that never took a full update. Note also this means the update disk rewrites the TABLE DATA too, so IC1/IC3 are not mask ROM as kn5000.cpp:1469-1470 implies.
hypothesis_verdicts.discriminating_test: Decompress the 'Program DATA FILE 1/2 + 2/2' SLIDE streams from the KN5000 v10 update disk set and compare byte-for-byte with kn5000_v10_program.rom. Identical => the ROM file is the update payload (and we should say so, and hunt for a resident block above it). Different anywhere => it is a genuine chip read. Same test for kn5000_table_data.rom vs the SLIDE4K stream at kn5000_v10_disk.img:0x4800 (header size field 0x200000 = 2 MB = exactly the table-data image).

hypothesis_verdicts.hypothesis: There is a region-4-only board variant with a second flash device at 0x380000, and MAME cannot reach it.
hypothesis_verdicts.reasoning: Three independent firmware signals, all region-gated, and MAME's AREA port literally cannot select region 4. Detect_Region_Code (v10/maincpu/shared/boot_routines.s:40-56) reads SFR 0x44 bits 2 and 1: 11->Region1, 10->Region2, 01->Region3, 00->Region4. kn5000.cpp:814-818 offers only PORT_DIPSETTING 0x02/0x04/0x06 — Region 4 (0x00) has NO setting, so that code path has never run in the emulator. The region-4 branches: (i) Flash_EraseSectorWithBankSelect (v10/maincpu/boot/system_handlers.s:6171+) adds 0x80000 to the command base when Get_Region_Code==4 AND target>=0x380000 — i.e. a second AMD-style device whose unlock cycles are relative to 0x380000; (ii) Flash_ChipErase issues a whole second unlock sequence at `lda_24 xiz, (0x380000)` under the same region==4 condition; (iii) the HD-AE5000 factory init is called only 'when region code != 4' (table_data/kn5000_table_data.s:3466). Sector arithmetic elsewhere in the same routine (add 0x70000/0xF0000, boot blocks at +0x78000/+0x7A000/+0x7C000 and +0xF8000) is consistent with a 1 MB top-boot part for regions 1-3 and a 512 KB top-boot part pair for region 4.
hypothesis_verdicts.discriminating_test: Ask Felipe for the model suffix on his unit's rating plate and, if he can power it, the value of the AREA strap bits — the MAME dip list maps Brazil to 0x02 (=Region 3), so if he is Region 3 this branch is irrelevant to his dump. Independently: check the service-manual parts list / SM page 32 for a second flash designator adjacent to IC19.

hypothesis_verdicts.hypothesis: The HD-AE5000 window at 0x280000 is a flat 512 KB ROM as MAME models it.
hypothesis_verdicts.reasoning: The firmware treats it as BANKED. HANDLE_UPDATE_FILE_TYPE_ID_006h ('Technics KN5000 HD-AEPRG DATA FILE', v10/maincpu/boot/system_handlers.s:7745-7752) writes to `xde = 0x280000` — so 0x280000 is the HD-AE5000 firmware flash, which also explains the 'bank 0 = 0x280000 / bank 1 = 0x300000' parameter of Flash_EraseSectorWithBankSelect. table_data/kn5000_table_data.s:3410-3446 (Flash_ProgramHDAE_Payload) selects a bank by writing the bank number to the 8255 PPI port at 0x160000, then copies 0x20000 bytes into 0x280000, for banks 4..7 (and 0..3 in the sibling routine) — 8 x 128 KB = 1 MB through the window, sourced from table data at 0x800000. The handoff then reads a 'hkt_' signature (0x5F746B68) at 0x2FFFC0 with bank 7 selected (kn5000_table_data.s:3567-3571). MAME's src/devices/bus/technics/kn5000/hdae5000.cpp:118 does `map(0x280000, 0x2fffff).rom().region(m_rom, 0)` — flat, read-only, no bank register.
hypothesis_verdicts.discriminating_test: Force the factory path: with the hdae5000 card fitted, breakpoint the 0x2FFFC0 read in HDAE5000_InitializeParallelPort and check whether MAME returns 0x5F746B68. If it does with a flat map, the banking is a superset never exercised; if it does not, the bank register at 0x160000 must be modelled.

hypothesis_verdicts.hypothesis: The unconditional 320 KB transfer from table_data 0x830000-0x87FFFF matches the v142 sub-CPU payload generation.
hypothesis_verdicts.reasoning: Nobody has checked the OTHER 62% of the sub-CPU image. SubCPU_Send_Payload sends five unconditional 64 KB blocks from 0x830000-0x87FFFF to sub-CPU 0x50000-0x8FFFF BEFORE the conditional 192 KB. I measured table_data file 0x30000 (= 0x830000): `ffffffff 00010000 001b0000 995a0200 996202 00 bdfe0300 996a0200 ...` — a table of 32-bit LE values 0x00000100, 0x00001B00, 0x00025A99, 0x00026299, 0x0003FEBD, 0x00026A99, 0x0002F803, 0x00029D95 ... every one of which lands inside the sub-CPU RAM range 0xF000-0x3EF00 that the v142 payload fills. So it IS sub-CPU material, not preset data. But if table_data (IC1/IC3) and the v142 PCK are from different firmware generations, this 320 KB half of the sub-CPU image is silently mismatched in the emulator and nobody would notice.
hypothesis_verdicts.discriminating_test: Take the ~20 pointer values at table_data 0x830004..0x830040 and check, in kn5000_subprogram_v142.rom, whether each target address (minus the 0xF000 load base, i.e. file offset = addr - 0xF000 + 0x100) begins with a plausible function prologue. High hit rate => matched pair; low hit rate => the table_data dump and the v142 payload are from different generations.

hypothesis_verdicts.hypothesis: The KN7000/KN6000 siblings can corroborate or contradict the KN5000 flash/CS arrangement.
hypothesis_verdicts.reasoning: They cannot — wrong CPU family. KN6000 and KN6500 are configurations of kn7000.cpp (kn7000.cpp:2121 kn6000(), :2182 kn6500()), i.e. MN10300 with a 32-bit linear map at 0x48400000 and an entirely different flash scheme (read view 0x56000000 / command view 0x96800000). There are no MSAR/MAMR/BnCS registers there at all. The ONLY TLCS-900 sibling in the tree is kn1500.cpp (TMP95C061), and notes/kn1500-lcd.md:45 already cites a 'crt0 chip-select setup' — that IS a usable comparison and nobody made it.
hypothesis_verdicts.discriminating_test: Diff the KN1500 crt0's MSAR/MAMR/BnCS writes against KN5000 boot_hw_init.s:85-134. If the KN1500 uses the same 'catch-all CS5 + external 138/139 decode' idiom, it confirms this is the house style and that IC19 cannot be relocated by register writes.

hypothesis_verdicts.hypothesis: Candidate A (table_data 0x800100) is simply a broken/impossible path.
hypothesis_verdicts.reasoning: More likely a LEGACY path for an earlier board generation, which reframes the whole puzzle. The chooser is a two-way switch selected by one flash byte; on every firmware we hold that byte is 0xFF and candidate A is never taken. Its source layout (xiz+0x100 for 192 KB, xiz+0x00 for the 0x100 trampoline block) is identical to candidate B's, and the unconditional part of the SAME routine already reads sub-CPU material out of table_data at 0x830000. That is exactly what you would expect if the sub-CPU program originally lived entirely in the table-data mask ROM at 0x800100-0x82FFFF and was later moved to updatable flash, with 0x800100-0x82FFFF reused for preset banks. No investigator raised this; the repo's own comment (table_data/kn5000_table_data.s:245-248) flags the area as unresolved.
hypothesis_verdicts.discriminating_test: One byte, in a file we do not yet have: read offset 0x1FFEED of kn5000_v5_program.rom (CRC 0xfbd035e3) or kn5000_v6_program.rom (CRC 0x0205db30). Non-FF on an early version proves the legacy-path reading and closes the question.

hypothesis_verdicts.hypothesis: The service manual has been consulted for the chip-select / decode wiring.
hypothesis_verdicts.reasoning: Only for ADDRESS lines, never for chip selects. kn5000.cpp:1494-1500 cites 'service manual page 32, CPU SECTION (A) P.C. Diagram' but only to argue IC14's AD_k <- net A(k+1) wiring is straight. No note in kn7000_mame/notes/ records the KN5000 decode network. The manual at /home/fsanches/compartilhado/technics-docs/service_manual/technics_sx-kn5000.pdf has NO text layer at all (pdftotext yields 0 lines; 59 CCITT/bitonal page images, pages 27-48 at 600 dpi, 9921x7008), which is presumably why. I rendered it and read the decode network for the first time: IC5 = TMP94C241F; bottom row IC1 (table data ODD), IC3 (table data EVEN), IC4 (program ODD), IC6 (program EVEN), IC9/IC10 (M5M44260AJ DRAM), IC14 (QSIGX3C23011, 32 Mbit), IC19 (QVIGFKN5KAX1, 8 Mbit CUSTOM DATA ROM); decoders IC11 TC74VHC138F (A18:A16, enables /CS2//CS3/CS1), IC12 T7W139F (A19), IC13 TC74VHC139F dual (A22, A20, A19).
hypothesis_verdicts.discriminating_test: Finish the trace on the crops already produced: follow IC19 pin12 (/CE) and pin14 (/OE), IC14's /CE, and IC11 pins 4 and 6 to their drivers, and record the result in kn7000_mame/notes/. That is the physical ground truth for the whole CS question and it is one afternoon of image work.

refuted_findings.claim: A text grep for writes to the chip-select registers in v10/maincpu found NOTHING (weak evidence, operands may be hidden in packed macros).
refuted_findings.why: The writes are plain, unpacked, and fully decoded — the grep used the wrong number base. /home/fsanches/compartilhado/kn5000-roms-disasm/v10/maincpu/shared/boot_hw_init.s:85-134 programs MSAR0-5, MAMR0-5, B0CSL-B5CSL and B0CSH-B5CSH as `stdi8 (<decimal>), <decimal>`, e.g. `stdi8 (339), 128; Block 4 @ 0x800000 (Table Data)` = MSAR4(0x153) := 0x80. Same file exists verbatim in v7, v9 and table_data/shared/.

refuted_findings.claim: 'The payload-source marker byte differs across firmware versions — that would be decisive.'
refuted_findings.why: It does not differ. kn5000_v7_program.rom, kn5000_v9_program.rom and kn5000_v10_program.rom all contain `ff ff ff 00 ff` at file offset 0x1FFEEB (CPU 0xFFFEEB). The two guards therefore evaluate identically in all three: 0xFFFEEF=0xFF (transfer proceeds) and 0xFFFEED=0xFF (IC19 path taken). The routine bodies are byte-equivalent too (v7:313-356 vs v10:316-359 differ only in symbolisation).

The firmware puts table data on CS4, not CS2. boot_hw_init.s:89 `stdi8 (339), 128` sets MSAR4 = 0x80 with the comment 'Block 4 @ 0x800000 (Table Data)'; CS2 is MSAR2 = 0xC0 (Block 2 @ 0xC00000) and is the block that gets remapped to 0x80 at the boot handoff. Related: calling IC1/IC3 'ROMs' understates them — update-disk file type 003h ('Technics KN5000 Table DATA FILE 1/2', system_handlers.s:7714-7724) runs Flash_BurnWithProgress against them, and the v10 update disk carries a SLIDE4K stream at 0x4800 whose header size field is 0x200000 = the full 2 MB table image.

refuted_findings.claim: table_data/kn5000_table_data.s:246-247 — 'If decompression fails, firmware falls back to data at 0x830000.'
refuted_findings.why: Wrong address. On SLIDE failure the code executes `ld xiz, 0x800000` (kn5000_v10_program.s:356) and the transfers read from xiz+0x100 = 0x800100. 0x830000 is the start of the FIVE UNCONDITIONAL 64 KB transfers that always run, regardless of which candidate is chosen.

refuted_findings.claim: table_data/kn5000_table_data.s:3822 — 'Sets up source address (0x3E0000 = Table Data ROM)'.
refuted_findings.why: 0x3E0000 is the IC19 custom-data flash (CS5 region 0x300000-0x3FFFFF), not table data. Table data is at 0x800000-0x9FFFFF after the CS2 remap. The routine's own code proves it: `lda_24 xwa, (0x300000); add xwa, 0xE0000`.

refuted_findings.claim: 'The emulator only works because kn5000.cpp does ROMX_LOAD of a file extracted from a system UPDATE FLOPPY, overlaid on a blank region. It is a reconstruction, not a chip image.' — implying the overlay is a guess.
refuted_findings.why: True as to provenance, but it is not a guess: it is the exact byte string the firmware itself writes to that exact address. HANDLE_UPDATE_FILE_TYPE_ID_007h ('Technics KN5000 Program DATA FILE PCK') erases IC19 sectors 0x3E0000 and 0x3F0000 then LZSS-decompresses into them (v10/maincpu/boot/system_handlers.s:7758-7770); and kn5000_subprogram_v142_compressed.rom is a contiguous byte-exact 0x16C13-byte extraction from kn5000_v10_disk.img at offset 0xF03A9, which is the PCK file named at 0x4200 of that same disk. Address and content are both correct; only the *acquisition path* is indirect.

refuted_findings.claim: 'The KN7000 and KN6000 siblings may reveal the same or a different flash/CS arrangement.'
refuted_findings.why: KN6000/KN6500 are MN10300 configurations of kn7000.cpp (kn7000.cpp:2121, :2182) with no TLCS-900 memory controller and no MSAR/MAMR/BnCS registers; their flash idiom is a separate read view / command view (0x56000000 / 0x96800000). There is nothing to compare. The only TLCS-900 sibling is kn1500.cpp (TMP95C061).

refuted_findings.claim: kn5000.cpp:1466 — IC30 'Ranges fe0800-ff7800 and ff9800-fff000 not dumped yet. Assumed here as being filled with 0xFF.'
refuted_findings.why: Not false, but misleading about what we actually have. The file's only non-FF content is CPU 0xFF8000-0xFF904C (4173 bytes) and 0xFFFE80-0xFFFFFF (384 bytes) — 4352 of 131072 bytes, 3.3%. So roughly 10 KB of the ranges the comment says WERE dumped are also 0xFF and are indistinguishable in the file from the ranges that were not. The comment should record the two blocks that carry data, not the two ranges that do not.

verdicts.notes:
SINGLE BIGGEST MISS, ranked: (1) the chip-select programming exists and is fully decoded at kn5000-roms-disasm/v10/maincpu/shared/boot_hw_init.s:85-134 (decimal operands defeated the grep); (2) the dynamic memory map is PROVEN and already documented in-repo — table_data/kn5000_table_data.s:1253-1258 writes MSAR2(0x14B):=0x80 and jumps to 0xFFFEDC, and table_data/boot_clib.s:7-9 states 'At reset the table-data ROM is mapped at 0xE00000-0xFFFFFF; after the CS2 remap it appears at 0x800000-0x9FFFFF'; (3) the IC19 payload chain is closed end-to-end (update-disk PCK file -> Flash_EraseSectorWithBankSelect 0x3E0000/0x3F0000 -> LZSS_Decompress_ToFlash), and kn5000_subprogram_v142_compressed.rom is a byte-exact contiguous extract from kn5000_v10_disk.img@0xF03A9; (4) the service manual's decode network (IC11/IC12/IC13) had never been read.

WHAT THIS DOES TO THE FRAMING: the puzzle is NOT 'where is the payload'. It is 'why is our IC19 dump blank exactly in the two sectors the firmware erases and rewrites'. Candidate A is a legacy path, not a live one. Felipe's dynamic-map intuition is correct as a phenomenon but probably wrong as the explanation for IC19 specifically, because CS5 is a catch-all (MSAR5=0x00 / MAMR5=0xFF) and IC19's window is fixed by external decode.

BYTE-GROUNDED BOOT-ORDER CONSTRAINT nobody stated: SubCPU_Send_Payload's first guard reads 0xFFFEEF, which is 0xFF in the program flash but 0x00 in the table-data ROM. Since real machines do ship the payload, the CS2 remap must already have happened when SubCPU_Send_Payload runs. Any future model of the dynamic map must satisfy this.

docs.summary:
Published the wave-6 investigation to the technics-docs site in five granular commits, each gated on a passing Jekyll build, with confidence grades carried through verbatim (proven / strong / plausible / undecided) and nothing upgraded.

NEW PAGES (3):
1. tmp94c241-memory-controller.md — the six programmable CS blocks, the measured register values from all six ROM images, the one runtime change (MSAR2 := 0x80 at table-data 0x9FB6D3), the +0x600000 boot alias, the IVT swap, the sub-CPU Port-G DRAM strap, and the fact that MAME stores MSAR/MAMR/BnCS and never consults them. The MSAR/MAMR decode rule is presented explicitly as a RECONSTRUCTION, not a reading: the page states that no datasheet exists here, that two mutually incompatible calibrations each claimed exact confirmation from the same MAME map, and that only the CS2 swap is established while every window boundary is provisional. Reset defaults and the /CS-to-IC assignment are marked unknown. Linked from hardware-architecture.md, memory-map.md and cpu-subsystem.md as required.
2. subcpu-payload-provenance.md — written for someone with no prior context: the transfer mechanism, the three marker bytes (FF FF FF 00 FF in v7/v9/v10), both candidate sources, what our dumps actually contain, the proven end-to-end update-floppy chain, all five hypotheses with verdicts (H1 SUPPORTED, H2 REFUTED, H3 UNDECIDED and split into three variants, H4 REFUTED, H5 SUPPORTED for the v10 BIOS only), and a costed table of the measurements that would settle each.
3. mame-emulation-gaps.md — the three prerequisites (FDC container formats, real flash devices, dynamic memory map) with an explicit dependency graph, the intelfsh16 byte-swap trap, the note that MAME already has an exact-match AMD 29F800B 16-bit device, and two exact acceptance tests.

UPDATED: rom-reconstruction.md and subcpu-firmware-images.md carry the dump-provenance record stated as owner testimony (IC30 partially dumped on purpose, 14,336 B read / 116,736 B assumed 0xFF / only 3.3% real data, educated guess not measurement, full dump intended); boot-sequence.md, system-update-discs.md, custom-data-flash.md, lzss-compression.md, subcpu-payload-loading.md corrected and qualified; reverse-engineering.md and ssf-presentation.md fixed where they called the IC30 0xFF region erased padding or blamed sequencer failures on "corruption in the undumped ranges".

INDEPENDENT VERIFICATION: I re-measured every load-bearing byte from the ROMs before writing — the handover instruction bytes, the 0xFFFED4 divergence between the two images, an exhaustive CS-register scan of all six images (26/26/26/24/0/0, reproducing the investigation), the IC30 non-FF block boundaries, the ten IC19 alignment anchors, and the update floppy. I also wrote my own SLIDE4K decoder and confirmed both disc streams decode byte-exactly.

ONE CORRECTION TO THE INVESTIGATION: it listed "is kn5000_v10_program.rom a chip read or a floppy payload?" as open and untested. The test has effectively been performed — the disc stream declares 0x200000 and decodes to the ROM byte for byte, and the update chip-erases the pair, so no region is left uncovered and the KN7000-style blind spot does not exist. I documented that as a measurement rather than repeating it as an open worry.

CONSTRAINTS HONOURED: only technics-docs was written to; the disassembly and MAME repos were read but never modified and no git command was run in them; the 39 pre-existing uncommitted flowcharts/ edits were never staged, reverted or mentioned; git add used explicit paths only; nothing was pushed.

WAVE6-PLAN.md was written (not committed) at /home/fsanches/.claude/jobs/d0e1b1c2/tmp/wave6/WAVE6-PLAN.md in the style of the binclude-audit PLAN.md: settled facts, overturned claims, the one genuinely open question, 11 hardware/external asks (3 free and blocking), and 19 analysis packages in four groups with an explicit ordering and two "do not start X before Y" rules.
